KEKERASAI.I

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency is Musi Rawas Regency;

2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Rawas Regency; 4
3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Rawas.
4. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is a guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence.
6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person holding control over another person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death
10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Women in conflict with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties.
14. Child is a person under the age of 18 years, including those in the womb.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
12. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child.
18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental barriers so as to interfere with his or her growth and development properly.
20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent. 21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of the child, into the family environment of the adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination.
22. Foster child is a child who is cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because his or her parents or one of his or her parents is unable to guarantee the child's proper growth and development.
23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with the religion professed and the child's abilities, talents, and interests.
24. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state.
25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
28. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim is about to occur, is occurring or has occurred.
29. Recovery of victims is all efforts to strengthen victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically.
30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor. 32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
33. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of domestic violence to resolve the problems faced.
34. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
35. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated method among recovery implementers in providing services to recover victims of domestic violence.
36. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
37. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
38. Every person is an individual or corporation. 39. Household is family members, relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandparents, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

Article 4
translated_text:
Article 4

The purpose of establishing this Regional Regulation is to provide protection and services to women and children victims of gender-based violence and in the best interests of children occurring in the household and/or public sphere, as well as to guarantee the fulfillment of children's rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination, for the realization of Indonesian children who are of quality, noble character, and prosperous.

CHAPTER III

Article 6

The Regency government and the Regency community are obligated and responsible to implement efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence, in the form of:

CHAPTER IV

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

1. For the implementation of protection for women and children, the Regency government is obligated to provide services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and facilitating the operation of integrated service institutions for victims involving community elements; and
b. encouraging community awareness of the importance of protection for victims.
2. The Regency government in carrying out the obligations as referred to in paragraph (1), must pay attention to the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons legally responsible for victims.
3. The implementation of Protection Institutions for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the P.ZTP2,A- framework.
4. Further provisions regarding P2IflP2,A are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 11
Article 12
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF CHILD PROTECTION

Bagian kesattr

Religion

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

Every child receives protection to worship according to (1) their religion.

Before a child can determine their choice, the religion held by (2) the child follows the religion of their parents.

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

1. The state, government, society, family, parents, guardians, and social institutions guarantee the protection of children in embracing their religion.
2. Protection of children in embracing their religion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes guidance, counseling, and practice of religious teachings for children.

Bagtan Kedua Kesehatan

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

1. The Government is obligated to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health efforts for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

2. The provision of facilities and organization of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

3. Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts, both for basic health services and referrals'.

4. Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are organized in cuilra-cuilra.

5. Implementation of the provisions as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), paragraph (3), and paragraph (4) is adjusted to the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

1. Parents and families are responsible for maintaining children's health and caring for children from the womb.
2. In the event that parents and families are unable to carry out the responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), then the government is obligated to fulfill them.
3. The obligations as referred to in paragraph (2), their implementation is carried out in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

The state, government, family, and parents are obliged to ensure that children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten their survival and/or cause disability.

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

1. The state, government, family, and parents are obliged to protect children from attempts to transplant the child’s body organs for other parties.
2. The state, government, family, and parents are obliged to protect children from acts of:
a. removal of children's body organs and/or children's body tissue without regard to the child's health;
b. buying and selling of children's organs and/or body tissue; and
c. health research that uses children as research objects without parental consent and does not prioritize the best interests of the child.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Education

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

The government is obliged to provide basic education of at least 9 (nine) years for all children.

heading: Article 2O
translated_text:
Article 2O

The state, government, family, and parents are obliged to provide the widest possible opportunity for children to obtain education.

heading: Article 21.
Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

Children with physical and/or mental disabilities are given equal opportunity and accessibility to obtain regular education and special education.

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

Children who have excellence are given opportunity and accessibility to obtain special education.

The government is responsible for providing education costs:

(1) and/or free assistance or special services for children from underprivileged families, neglected children, and children residing in remote areas.

The government's responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1):

(2) also includes encouraging the community to play an active role. 15

heading: Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

Children inside and in the school environment must be protected from acts of violence committed by teachers, school administrators or their friends in the school concerned, or other educational institutions.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Social

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. The government is obliged to provide care and maintenance for neglected children, both in institutions and outside institutions.
2. The provision of care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by community institutions.
3. To provide care and maintenance for neglected children, government institutions and community institutions, as referred to in paragraph (2), may cooperate with various related parties.
4. In the case of providing care and maintenance as referred to in paragraph (3), it is carried out by the Social Service.

heading: Article 27
Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

In the event that a child is neglected because for some reason the parents neglect their obligations, then the institution as referred to in Article 27, family, or authorized official may submit an application to the court to determine the child as a neglected child.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

1. The court determination as referred to in Article 4O simultaneously determines the place of shelter, care, and maintenance for the neglected child concerned.
2. The government or authorized institution is obliged to provide a place as referred to in paragraph (1).

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Special Protection

heading: Article 3O
translated_text:
Article 3O

The government and other state institutions are obliged and responsible to provide special protection to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (napza) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of mistreatment and neglect.

heading: Article 31
Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

Special protection for children who become refugees as referred to in Article 30 letter a is implemented in accordance with the provisions of humanitarian law.

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

Special protection for children who are victims of unrest, disaster victims, and children in armed conflict situations as referred to in Article 3O letter b, letter c, and letter d, is implemented through:

a. fulfillment of basic needs consisting of food, clothing, housing, education, health, learning and recreation, security guarantees, and equal treatment; and

b. fulfillment of special needs for children with disabilities and children experiencing psychosocial disorders.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

Everyone is prohibited from recruiting or using children for military and/or other interests and leaving children without protection for their lives.

heading: Article 35
Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

1. Special protection for children from minority and isolated groups as referred to in Article 30 shall be carried out through the provision of infrastructure and facilities to enable them to enjoy their own culture, profess and practice their own religion, and use their own language.
2. Every person is prohibited from obstructing children as referred to in paragraph (1) from enjoying their own culture, professing and practicing their own religion, and using their own language without neglecting access to community and cultural development.

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

1. Special protection for children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 30 is the obligation and responsibility of the government and society.
2. Special protection for children who are exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:
a. Dissemination and/or socialization of provisions of laws and regulations related to the protection of children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various government agencies, companies, labor unions, non-governmental organizations, and the community in the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of children.
3. Every person is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering the commission of, or participating in the exploitation of children as referred to in paragraph (1).

heading: Article 38
translated_text:
Article 38

1. Special protection for children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances (napza) abuse as referred to in Article 30, and involved in their production and distribution, shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation efforts by the government and society.
2. Every person is prohibited from intentionally placing, allowing, involving, ordering the involvement of children in the abuse, production and distribution of napza as referred to in paragraph (1).

heading: Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

1. Special protection for child victims of abduction, sale, and trafficking of children as referred to in Article 30 shall be carried out through supervision, protection, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation efforts by the government and society.
2. Every person is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering the commission of, or participating in abduction, sale, or trafficking as referred to in paragraph (1).

heading: Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

(1) Special protection for child victims of violence as referred to in Article 30 includes physical, psychological, and sexual violence, carried out through efforts of dissemination and socialization of provisions of laws and regulations that protect child victims of violence; and monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions.

(2) Every person is prohibited from placing, allowing, committing, ordering the commission of, or participating in violence as referred to in paragraph (1).

heading: Article 41
translated_text:
Article 41

Special protection for children with disabilities as referred to in Article 30 shall be carried out through efforts:

a. treatment of children in a humane manner in accordance with the dignity and rights of the child;
b. fulfillment of special needs; and
c. obtaining equal treatment with other children to achieve full social integration and individual development as much as possible.

Every person is prohibited from treating children by disregarding their views in a discriminatory manner, including labeling and equalization in education for children with disabilities.

heading: Article 42
translated_text:
Article 42

(1) Special protection for child victims of abuse and neglect as referred to in Article 30 shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation by the government and society.

(2) Every person is prohibited from placing, allowing, involving, ordering the involvement of children in situations of abuse and neglect as referred to in paragraph (1).

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN

Rights of Women

heading: Article 51
translated_text:
Article 51

Women have the right to obtain education and training in employment, positions, and professions in accordance with the requirements that have been determined.

heading: Article 52
translated_text:
Article 52

1. Women have the right to choose, be elected, be appointed, in employment, positions, and professions in accordance with the requirements and provisions of legislation.
2. Women have the right to obtain special protection in the implementation of their work or profession against matters that may threaten their safety and or health in connection with the reproductive function of Women.
3. Special rights attached to Women due to their reproductive function are guaranteed and protected by law.

heading: Article 53
translated_text:
Article 53

Women who are adults and or are married have the right to perform legal acts independently, unless otherwise determined by their religious law.

heading: Article 54
translated_text:
Article 54

In the examination of cases of Women in Contact with the Law, judges must not:

a. show an attitude or issue statements that demean, blame and/or intimidate Women in Contact with the Law.

b. justify the occurrence of Discrimination Against Women by using culture, customary rules and other traditional practices or by using expert interpretations that are Gender biased;

c. question and/or consider the experience or sexual background of the victim as a basis for acquitting the perpetrator or mitigating the punishment of the perpetrator; and

d. issue statements or views that contain Gender stereotypes.

heading: Article 55
translated_text:
Article 55

During the course of trial examination, judges shall prevent and/or reprimand the parties, legal advisors, public prosecutors and/or legal counsel who behave or make statements that demean, blame, intimidate and/or use the experience or sexual background of Women in Contact with the Law.

heading: Article 56
translated_text:
Article 56

If Women in Contact with the Law experience physical and psychological obstacles requiring assistance, the Judge may grant the request of Women in Contact with the Law to present a Companion.

heading: Article 57
translated_text:
Article 57

The judge on his or her own initiative and or at the request of the parties, public prosecutor, legal advisor and/or victim may order Women in Contact with the Law to have their testimony heard through examination by remote audio visual communication at the local court or at another place, if:

1. The mental/psychological condition of Women in Contact with the Law is unhealthy due to fear/psychological trauma based on the assessment of a doctor or psychologist;

2. Based on the judge's assessment, the safety of Women in Contact with the Law is not guaranteed if they are in a public and open place; or

3. Based on the decision of the Witness and Victim Protection Agency (LPSK), Women in Contact with the Law are declared to be in the witness and/or victim protection program according to LPSK and cannot attend the trial to give testimony either for security reasons or due to physical and psychological obstacles.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

ROLE OF THE COMMUNITY

Article 58

1. The community has the right to obtain the widest possible opportunity to participate in the protection of women and children.
2. The role of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, child protection institutions, community social institutions, community self-reliance institutions, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities, and mass media.

heading: Article 59
translated_text:
Article 59

The role of the community is implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable legislation.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

IMPLEMENTATION OF VICTIM RECOVERY

Article 60

1. The implementation of recovery activities for women and child victims includes:

a. Health services;

Health services are carried out by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.

b. Victim assistance;

Victim assistance is carried out by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, therapy, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims.

c. Counseling;

Counseling is provided by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.

d. Spiritual guidance;

Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.

e. Resocialization.

Resocialization of victims is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 61

Any person who intentionally does not provide protection for women and children such that:

a. causes violence to occur;

b. allows violence to occur; and/or

c. does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of legislation.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 62

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered with its placement in the Regional Gazette of Musi Rawas Regency.

heading: EXPLANATION
translated_text:
EXPLANATION

REGIONAL REGULATION OF MUSI RAWAS REGENCY

NUMBER T. YEAR 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

GENERAL

I. The National Objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as regulated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph are stated to include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and the entire territory of Indonesia, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on: (a) independence, (b) eternal peace, and (c) social justice. To achieve these objectives, in accordance with the doctrine of trias politica, there are three State powers namely executive power for the administration of government, legislative power as the formulator of laws and regulations and judicial power as the implementer of laws and regulations. In Indonesia, these three powers complement each other, for the implementation of a clean and authoritative government, from the national level to the regional level.

The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a State of Power (machtstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The Rights of Women and Children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.

Regional Autonomy that is implemented, has strategic value so that each region forms legislation (Regional Regulations), not only to express local wisdom, but also to become a guideline for Regional Governments to implement the legislation above it (the 1945 Constitution, and Laws) to address legal problems and social problems that occur specifically in each region.

This Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children, is based on Pancasila, and the 1945 Constitution, and refers to Laws that regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence, among others are Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 29 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 11 of 2012 concerning Juvenile Justice System, Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 1 of 2016 concerning Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection into Law, and other related Laws, Law Number 8 of 2016 concerning Persons with Disabilities, Supreme Court Regulation Number 3 of 2017 concerning Guidelines for Adjudicating Cases of Women Dealing with the Law, The principles of this Regional Regulation are principles contained in previous laws and regulations, for example the principle of respect for Human Rights and gender equality and justice, are actually already contained in

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

The 1945 Constitution, which essentially constitutes legal provisions on gender equality and justice, while simultaneously reflecting recognition of human rights, because what is referred to as every Citizen naturally consists of men and women, having equal standing in the field of law and government.

Also in Article 28 G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution which essentially stipulates that every person, naturally both men and women, has the right to protection and freedom from fear. Article 28H paragraph (2) which essentially regulates the right of citizens to obtain facilities and special treatment to obtain equality and justice, naturally including women and children victims of violence.

Violence whose victims are women and children occurs both within marriage and outside marriage. Whereas Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage, which in Article 1 regulates the definition of marriage as a physical and spiritual bond between a man and a woman to build a household based on the One Supreme God. Article 30 stipulates that the obligation of husband and wife is to be faithful to each other, love, and help.

In this Marriage Law, it is regulated regarding who becomes a biological child, as well as joint property, including the method of continuing its ownership or inheritance to the children. If this Law is complied with, it can prevent and eliminate Domestic Violence, unfortunately what happens in society is that Domestic Violence (KDRT) is increasingly rampant, precisely with increasingly complex modus operandi and causing increasingly horrific consequences. The principle of non-discrimination is in line with the recognition of human rights, therefore it is very appropriate that the Government of Indonesia by enacting Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW), in Article 1 states the definition of discrimination against women and all its consequences if discrimination against women occurs.

Basically working is only for adults, whereas children, namely people aged under 18 years, are obliged to study and play. However, due to family economic limitations, there are some children who must work. Therefore Law Number 20 of 1999, concerning the Minimum Age Limit for Children to be able to work by providing provisions that parents and employers should pay attention to the provisions of this Law, so that even though children are forced to work, they do not lose their youth and can still attend school to secure their future. Children who are forced to work are found in all areas, both in urban and rural areas. In order for children to obtain their rights, socialization of Law Number 20 of 1999 is urgent to be carried out.

As a consequence of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as a State that signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights is the answer. Considering that although since Indonesia's Independence, the 1945 Constitution also stated the recognition of human rights as regulated in Articles 27 to 34, in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence which clearly constitutes a violation of human rights. In Law Number 39 of 1999 it is reaffirmed that women's rights are human rights (Article 45) and Article 52 paragraph (2), which states that Children's rights are Human Rights and for the benefit of children's rights they are recognized and protected by law even from the womb.

This means that children are recognized as having freedom and liberty in accordance with their dignity as human beings, so that any form of violence whatsoever must not occur to children, because it constitutes a violation of Human Rights.

The commitment and political will of the Government of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia to protect children is reinforced by the enactment of Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection. In accordance with the types of crimes against children which are increasingly occurring today, we need to study the provisions of articles 77 to 90, which already provide sufficiently severe criminal sanctions (threats). Examples related to this regional regulation for cases occurring in society are those violating Articles 81, 82 and 83. For this reason, let us examine the contents of Articles 81, 82, 83 so that child victims of violence or sexual crimes in society receive legal protection in accordance with a sense of justice

heading: Article 81 states:
translated_text:
Article 81 states:

(1) Every person who intentionally commits violence or threat of violence forcing a child to have intercourse with him or with another person, shall be punished with imprisonment of a maximum of 15 (fifteen) years and a minimum of 5 (five) years and a fine of a maximum of Rp.300,000,000,- (three hundred million rupiah) and a minimum of Rp.5,000,000,000.- (Five Billion rupiah).

(2) The Criminal provisions as referred to in paragraph (1) also apply to every person who intentionally commits fraud, a series of lies, or persuades a child to have intercourse with him or with another person.

(3) The Criminal provisions as referred to in paragraph (1) if committed by Parents, Guardians, Child Caregivers, Educators or Education Personnel, then the sentence is increased by 1/3 (one third) of the sentence as referred to in paragraph (1)

(2) The Criminal provisions as referred to in paragraph (1) if committed by Parents, Guardians, Child Caregivers, Educators or Education Personnel, then the sentence is increased by 1/3 (one third) of the sentence as referred to in paragraph (1)
